newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 24.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor lost the opportunity of winning the second Test at Lord's on Monday when he dropped a straight-forward chance at first slip. Australia was leading by 136 on the first innings after dismissing England for 77 on Saturdy. Page 20.

Although the Perth Reds Super League team had a disastrous European tour, club chairman Stephen Edwards said he had received assurances from Super League heavyweights Ian Frykberg and Ken Cowley that the Reds position in the Super League or in a united competition is still secure for next year. Page 20.

World pole vault record-holder Emma George will return to Melbourne this week to recuperate after spraining her ankle during training in Germany. She will miss three competitions in Europe but will still compete in the World Student Games in Sicily later his year. Page 18.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

A disappointing crowd of 31,572 has prompted the Australian Rugby Union to review its ticket pricing. ARU chief executive John O'Neill admitted yesterday that they may be pricing themselves out of the market with price tags such as $62 for a ticket to the Wallaby Test against France at the Sydney Football Stadium. Page 46.

Twenty-seven-year-old South African Ernie Els has taken over Tiger Woods as the world No 1 ranking golf champion by winning the US Open. He also captured the Buick Classic on Sunday by two shots over American Jeff Maggert. Page 44.

The West Sydney Slammers basketball team hope a deal with the Canterbury Leagues Club will enable them to garner enough financial clout to gain admission to the National Basketball League. West Sydney is optimistic and has requested a meeting with the NBL board later this month. Page 43.
THE AGE

AFL Geelong champion centreman Paul Couch will announce his retirement today, completing Geelong's transformation from a high-scoring attacking outfit to a defensive unit. Couch managed only five games this year because of a painful cartilage deterioration in his knee. Page B12.

Australia's heavyweight rowing eight beat Olympic silver medalist Germany in a stunning victory at the Paris World Cup regatta. The Australian team also picked up gold in the lightweight eights, silver in the men's quad scull and men's lightweight coxlesspair as well as bronze in the men's double scull and women's pair. Page B10.

Australian Opals guard Michele Timms helped the Phoenix Mercury defeat the Charlotte Sting by scoring eight points in the new American Women's national Basketball League last night. The match drew the largest crowd ever to attend a women's professional game in the US. Page B10.
THE HERALD SUN

After dislocating his shoulder in the first round of the season against Melbourne, AFL champion forward Wayne Carey will be making his return at the North Melbourne-Sydney Grand Final rematch on Sunday. Page 70.

Melbourne's entire pool of available AFL players slipped off to a mid-season camp early this morning. The camp, at an undisclosed location, is designed to focus the players' minds on new goals for the remaining 10 rounds, beginning this Sunday at Waverley Park. Page 70.

Stakemoney for the AG Hunter Cup has been cut by $50,000. Dubbed the Melbourne Cup of harness racing, the Hunter cup will carry $400,000 at Moonee Valley on February 21 next year. Harness Racing Victoria chairman Ian McEwan has dismissed claims that the industry is cash-strapped. Page 69.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Super League warned that three more ARL clubs are preparing to defect unless a compromise is reached for next season. The defection will cause ARL to collapse and the $120 million Optus Vision funding package for the competition will be withdrawn. Page 64

Canterbury-Bankstown Leagues Club is planning to formally lodge an application to build a $150 million development at Liverpool's Woodward Park that will include a second Canterbury Leagues Club. The club will also be diversifying to include basketball, bseball and soccer. Page 62.

The Australian women's softball team won the six-nation Haarlem tournament yesterday after beating world No 2 China twice in the finals. The victory is sweet revenge for Australia who lost the Olympic silver medal to China last year. Page 61.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
